resources.string: Tutorial
Welcome to Space Compass
Explore the sky, follow celestial paths and preview other places and times. Discover the main controls with the interactive tutorial.
Touch a highlighted control or an orbit point to learn what it does. Controls are explained without changing your settings.
Zoom
Selected object
Orbit points
Open app information, release notes and source credits.
Open General, Language, Units, Tutorial and Info and credits.
Choose the objects to display. Search, filter and save favorites in the catalog.
Preview another position, altitude, time zone, date or time, and adjust how time advances.
Show celestial reference circles, poles, zenith and nadir. These are sky projections, not routes on the ground.
0–24 shows the whole calendar day, from midnight to midnight. +24h shows the next 24 hours from the displayed time, including a simulated time. Daily path, captures and exports use the same interval.

Switch between the simulated sky and the rear camera. The camera uses the real pointing axis. Here you can explore Zoom and Transparency without using the camera. Tap again to return to the normal view.
Show or hide weather effects in the simulated sky and panoramas. This control is unavailable in camera mode.
Choose the camera axis (90°) or the phone length axis (0°) for pointing. Camera mode always uses the camera axis.
Make object images more translucent to compare them with the camera view. The capture keeps this choice.
Choose the simulated sky zoom from 0.5× to 1×. In camera mode, use the available lens zoom or pinch the view. The two settings are saved separately.
Prepare a full-sky panorama, or capture the current camera view with celestial overlays. Export from the preview. In the preview, double-tap the image to show or hide the controls.
Collapse or expand the object and compass islands to gain sky space.
Tap to show or hide the opposite direction of selected points: azimuth +180° and elevation with the opposite sign. Hold to deselect all points.
Move through the selected objects. The island shows the active object and its trajectory colors.
Tap the object name to open the Observatory: model, scientific details, travel time, key heights and events. Its top bar contains Daily path, Export and Favorites, in that order.
Open the active object’s trajectory, times, elevations and selectable points. Future events can have reminders.
Open details of your real position, GPS altitude, orientation and weather. These values are independent of the Location.

Select or deselect an orbit point. Aim the reticle at a point to read its object, time, T, azimuth and elevation. The object border follows its trajectory colour; selecting its current position changes the border to blue or cyan.
Time and icons
Tap empty sky to pause or resume time. Double-tap to show or hide the reticle and icons.
Open Android’s alarm or calendar for an eligible future event. Past events and the current point cannot have an alarm.
Status and recovery
Read the current status. Its action can request permission, enable location or retry unavailable orbital or weather data. The tutorial does not execute the action.
Remove the active object from the selected objects after confirmation. The object remains available in the catalog.
